newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai govt set 1997 EU tapioca export 5.25 mln tns.
newsitem.headline: Thai govt set 1997 EU tapioca export 5.25 mln tns.

text.p: The Thai government on Tuesday set the 1997 tapioca export quota to the European Union at 5.25 million tonnes, unchanged from this year, a commerce ministry official said.
The government will maintain its control over the allocation of the export quota, the official said.
The export allocation will be based on the size of stocks exporters hold and a bonus system, he said.

Thailand, one of the world's biggest tapioca exporters, has an agreement with the EU to deliver a maximum of 21 million tonnes of tapioca pellets over four years between 1995-1998. A maximum of 5.5 million tonnes can be delivered in any single year.
With about 80-90 percent of all tapioca pellet exports going to the European Union, the government is now trying to encourage exporters to expand the market.
In order to encourage selling outside the EU, the government will award two tonnes of EU quota for any one tonne of tapioca exporters ship to non-EU markets, the official said.
Stock-checking will be carried out six times a year to force the exporters to keep stocks during harvest season to ensure high prices for fresh cassava roots to farmers, he said.

Thailand local tapioca pellet production has fallen short of the EU export quota in the past two years. The country is expected to export around 3.1 million tonnes of tapioca pellet for 1996, the official said. --Bangkok newsroom (662) 652-0642
